notes: Follow-up check on the 4 TRAKE queries in audio_ground_truth.json, run through
the REAL temporal_search.py pipeline (build_sequences DP + fuse_audio +
temporal_nms), not the whole-text-blob proxy used in earlier rounds -- that
proxy is not representative of production TRAKE handling. temporal_search.py
and app.py's temporal logic were NOT modified for this check (fair A/B).
3 of 4 queries have per-event gold timestamps in temporal_ground_truth.json
(query-p1-4, -16, -18); 2026:query-p1-16-trake (L24_V024) has none, gold-video
rank only, events hand-translated from its Vietnamese text.
Per-event localization is IDENTICAL across all 3 audio strategies for every
query -- the DP's event candidates are 100% visual (core.encode_texts + FAISS
flat index), so no audio chunking strategy can change which frame is picked
per event. Audio only nudges the whole-sequence RANK via fuse_audio's RRF
(window_seconds=30, hardcoded in temporal_search.fuse_audio, separate from
app.fuse_search_results' adaptive window). The wide audio-evidence spans
reported below (150-330s) come from merge_temporal_hits chaining multiple
overlapping same-video passages together -- this happens identically for the
sliding baseline (E) too, so it is not evidence of semantic chunks themselves
being 150-330s long, nor of them merging distinct TRAKE events.

per_event_correct_of_4.2025:query-p1-4-trake: 1/4 (identical across all 3 -- visual localization is imperfect for this query independent of audio)
per_event_correct_of_4.2025:query-p1-16-trake: 2/4 (identical across all 3; near-silent lion-dance video, no audio evidence in any config)

trake_check.verdict: No meaningful regression. One video (2025:query-p1-16-trake, near-silent) moves one rank worse (5->6) with C, but audio contributes nothing to any of the 3 configs for that video (source=visual-only throughout) -- the difference is noise/tie-breaking among visual-only paths, not a chunking effect. The one TRAKE video with real narration (2025:query-p1-18-trake) improves under C (rank 2->1 vs sliding, 3->1 vs A) because C's matching passage scored the best audio_rank (1, vs sliding's 2 and A's 18). C is confirmed as the global default.

notes: Phase 2. Fixed config C (min=10/target=40/max=75/window=3/percentile=15/overlap=1)
throughout; only the pause mechanism varies. Same offline
BM25(LexicalIndex)+dense(DenseIndex)+RRF+merge_temporal_hits proxy and the real,
adaptive-window app.fuse_search_results as the runs above (Elasticsearch not
running in this environment). All 44 KIS/QA queries counted in every headline
number below -- no query is excluded from the primary metric, including
2026:query-p1-21-kis (see 'known_sensitive_query' below for why it swings hard).
Round 1 tested the ungated mechanism alone (any boundary with a long pause,
relative to that video's own pause distribution, became eligible -- no semantic
support required). Round 2 added a second, wider 'borderline semantic' percentile
(pause_borderline_semantic_percentile) and gated pause so it can only PROMOTE a
boundary that already clears that wider percentile, never manufacture one alone:
eligible = strong_semantic OR (borderline_semantic AND long_pause). Both rounds'
manual review sampled 'this boundary exists only because of pause' cases across
news, cooking, travel/documentary and sports content and read the surrounding
transcript by hand to judge whether each was a real topic transition.

ungated.description: strong_semantic OR pause_boosted, no borderline gate -- audio_search._assemble_bounded_chunks(..., borderline_candidates=None). Not reachable from any production CLI flag; kept only as a directly-callable code path for this historical ablation and any future re-benchmarking.
ungated.manual_boundary_review: 12 pause-only boundaries sampled across news/cooking/travel-documentary/sports (3 each). 6/12 (50%) read as real topic transitions on manual reading; false boundaries concentrated in interview-style news (0/3) and live sports commentary (~1/3), where a long pause is often just a breath/rhythm gap within the same continuing statement, not a topic change. Travel/documentary narration fared best (3/3).
ungated.verdict: Retrieval does not clearly regress (recall ties or slightly improves), but pause dominates 70-86% of all boundaries (pause_only + both) and roughly half of pause-only splits are false on manual review. Rejected as a production candidate: the mechanism overrides the semantic signal far more than it augments it.

gated.description: strong_semantic OR (borderline_semantic AND pause_boosted), where borderline_semantic is a second, wider _breakpoint_candidates call at pause_borderline_semantic_percentile (default 30.0). This is the only pause behavior reachable through make_bounded_semantic_passages / the production CLI flags when pause_boost_enabled=True.
gated.manual_boundary_review: 10 promoted-by-pause boundaries sampled across the same 4 content types. 7/10 (70%) read as real topic transitions -- a clear improvement over the ungated 50%. News remained the weakest category (1/4): most boundaries there still land within one continuing news item rather than at its actual end.
gated.known_sensitive_query: 2026:query-p1-21-kis (gold L22_V011, the 'tôm hùm/trang trí món ăn' query from the original hybrid-fusion investigation) swings hard under gating: hybrid rank 3->9, audio rank 17->82. Root-caused by hand: gating shifts the forced-split boundary near the matching passage by ~10s (from A's clean [453.4-525.5s] chunk to a [463.0-536.5s] chunk prefixed with less-relevant lead-in text), diluting the coincidental lexical overlap that gave this passage its (already marginal, rank ~17) audio match. Excluding only this one query from the hybrid recall computation: A/B 69.8/88.4/88.4 (R@1/5/10), gated-C 67.4/88.4/90.7, gated-D 67.4/88.4/88.4 -- R@5 and R@10 tie or beat pause-off once this single boundary-position-sensitive query is set aside, R@1 remains ~2pp behind (one further query, 2026:query-p1-22-kis, drops hybrid rank 1->2 on an unrelated top-of-list RRF tie-break with an unchanged audio rank). This query is NOT excluded from any headline recall number above -- it is the reason gated-C/D's R@1/R@5 read lower than pause-off in the headline table.

pause_boost_check.verdict: Gated pause-boost is implemented correctly (100% of promoted boundaries carry independent borderline-semantic evidence; total pause-influenced share of all boundaries drops from 85.6% ungated to 46.2%/37.5% gated) and clearly improves manual boundary quality (50% -> 70% real topic transitions). It does not, however, demonstrate a retrieval improvement over Phase 1 (pause off) large enough on this 44-query benchmark to justify the added complexity by itself -- the headline recall dip is dominated by one boundary-position-sensitive query, not a systemic effect, but 44 queries (~2.3 points each) cannot resolve that distinction with confidence. Decision: keep pause_boost_enabled=False as the production default; keep the gated implementation in the codebase as an optional, fully-tested feature for future re-benchmarking (e.g. against a larger ground truth) rather than shipping it now. The ungated mechanism is not a production candidate at all -- retained in audio_search._assemble_bounded_chunks only as a directly-callable path for historical ablation/testing, never reachable from make_bounded_semantic_passages or any CLI flag.
